import { existsSync, readFileSync, writeFileSync, mkdirSync, statSync } from 'node:fs'
import { resolve, join, extname } from 'node:path'
import { createHash } from 'node:crypto'
import { createServer } from 'node:http'
import { spawn } from 'node:child_process'
import { pathToFileURL } from 'node:url'
import { child } from './session-lifecycle.mjs'
import { livePreviewScript, watchProject } from './live-preview.mjs'

export function projectType(root) {
  if (existsSync(join(root, 'package.json'))) {
    const p = JSON.parse(readFileSync(join(root, 'package.json'), 'utf8'))
    if (p.dependencies?.next || p.devDependencies?.next) throw new Error('Unsupported framework: customize start.sh and provide static deployment output.')
    if (p.dependencies?.vite || p.devDependencies?.vite) return 'vite'
    throw new Error('Unsupported package project: customize start.sh and deployment output.')
  }
  if (existsSync(join(root, 'index.html'))) return 'html'
  throw new Error('No generated index.html or supported package project.')
}
export async function start(root = process.cwd()) {
  const type = projectType(root)
  const projectRoot = resolve(root)
  if (type === 'vite') {
    const stampDir = process.env.OPENCODE_WEB_DIR || join(root, 'node_modules', '.cache')
    mkdirSync(stampDir, { recursive: true })
    const stamp = join(stampDir, 'default-dependencies')
    const lock = join(root, 'package-lock.json')
    const hash = createHash('sha256').update(readFileSync(join(root, 'package.json'))).update(existsSync(lock) ? readFileSync(lock) : '').digest('hex')
    let old = ''
    try { old = readFileSync(stamp, 'utf8') } catch {}
    if (old !== hash || !existsSync(join(root, 'node_modules/vite'))) {
      await child('npm', [existsSync(lock) ? 'ci' : 'install', '--no-audit', '--no-fund'], { cwd: root })
      mkdirSync(stampDir, { recursive: true })
      const installedHash = createHash('sha256').update(readFileSync(join(root, 'package.json'))).update(existsSync(lock) ? readFileSync(lock) : '').digest('hex')
      writeFileSync(stamp, installedHash)
    }
    await child(process.execPath, [join(root, 'node_modules/vite/bin/vite.js'), 'build', '--base', './'], { cwd: root })
    root = join(root, 'dist')
  }
  if (!existsSync(join(root, 'index.html'))) throw new Error('Static deployment output must contain index.html.')
  if (process.env.OPENCODE_WEB_DIR) writeFileSync(join(process.env.OPENCODE_WEB_DIR, 'deployment-output.json'), JSON.stringify({ project: projectRoot, directory: resolve(root) }))
  const mime = { '.html':'text/html', '.js':'application/javascript', '.css':'text/css', '.json':'application/json', '.svg':'image/svg+xml', '.png':'image/png', '.jpg':'image/jpeg', '.webp':'image/webp', '.wasm':'application/wasm', '.glb':'model/gltf-binary' }
  const clients = new Set()
  const stopWatching = watchProject(root, () => { for (const client of clients) client.write('event: change\ndata: changed\n\n') })
  const keepAlive = setInterval(() => { for (const client of clients) client.write(': keepalive\n\n') }, 20000)
  const buildWatcher = type === 'vite' ? spawn(process.execPath, [join(projectRoot, 'node_modules/vite/bin/vite.js'), 'build', '--base', './', '--watch'], { cwd: projectRoot, stdio: 'inherit' }) : null
  const server = createServer((req, res) => {
    try {
      const url = new URL(req.url, 'http://localhost')
      if (url.pathname === '/__omgithub/live') {
        res.writeHead(200, { 'Content-Type': 'text/event-stream', 'Cache-Control': 'no-cache', 'X-Accel-Buffering': 'no', Connection: 'keep-alive' })
        res.write(': connected\n\n')
        clients.add(res)
        req.on('close', () => clients.delete(res))
        return
      }
      const path = resolve(root, '.' + decodeURIComponent(url.pathname))
      if (path !== resolve(root) && !path.startsWith(resolve(root) + '/')) { res.writeHead(404); res.end(); return }
      const file = statSync(path).isDirectory() ? join(path, 'index.html') : path
      res.setHeader('Content-Type', mime[extname(file)] || 'application/octet-stream')

      const content = readFileSync(file)
      if (extname(file) === '.html' && url.searchParams.get('omgithub_live') === '1') {
        const html = content.toString()
        res.end(/<\/body\s*>/i.test(html) ? html.replace(/<\/body\s*>/i, `${livePreviewScript}</body>`) : html + livePreviewScript)
      } else res.end(content)
    } catch { res.writeHead(404); res.end('Not found') }
  })
  server.on('close', () => { stopWatching(); clearInterval(keepAlive); buildWatcher?.kill(); for (const client of clients) client.end() })
  server.listen(Number(process.env.PORT || 3000), '0.0.0.0')
  return server
}

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build a polished, playable 2D browser game based on the prompt: “2D Vampire Survivors, but you play the horde”.
- The game is named **HORDE — The Last Night**; player commands a growing bat swarm, devours defenders, mutates on level-up, and kills the Dawnbringer before dawn.

## Requirements
- Self-contained browser game under the current repo; no external assets or frameworks.
- Static `index.html` served by the existing `start.sh` runtime.
- Responsive desktop/mobile support with touch controls.
- Polished title, gameplay HUD, level-up cards, pause, victory/defeat, sound, and restart flow.
- Use procedural canvas art, effects, particles, lighting, and audio.

## Decisions
- Reverse Survivors premise: horde count is both health and DPS; souls restore bats and grant XP.
- 3-minute run; boss **Dawnbringer** spawns at elapsed 120s, victory on boss kill, defeat on horde wipe or timer expiry.
- Controls: WASD/arrows, Space/right-side button for Blood Surge, Esc pause, mobile virtual joystick.
- Upgrades: Broodmother, Serrated Fangs, Blood Frenzy, Night Wings, Crimson Echo, Grave Hide, Carrion Feast, Blood Moon, Red Feast.
- Added larger world (`H.WW`, `H.WH`) with a following camera to avoid empty map edges, while title uses a separate screen-sized background.
- Reworked survivor art from top-down blobs into readable 3/4-view hooded hero sprites.

## Work State
### Completed
- Full static site and game implementation.
- Title screen, in-game HUD, level-up overlay, pause overlay, end screen, banners/toasts, best-score persistence, sound toggle.
- Procedural backdrop, fog, ambient motes, fire, particles, shockwaves, damage flashes, screen shake, boss bar.
- Core gameplay: swarm movement/auto-bite, survivor AI classes, projectiles, telegraphs, spawn waves, souls/XP, upgrades, boss phases, victory/defeat.
- Responsive CSS and mobile joystick/surge controls.
- Browser tested at 1440×900; title and gameplay screenshots captured successfully; no current console errors after fixing `lerp is not defined`.

### Active
- Final visual/performance polish and verification of all screens and mechanics.
- Need verify mobile layout and level-up/end overlays visually.
- Need verify boss encounter and victory/defeat flows.

### Blocked
- Headless Chromium renders at about **8 FPS** under SwiftShader, slowing real-time gameplay tests; this is software-rendering-specific, not necessarily representative of GPU browsers.

## Next Move
1. Inspect latest screenshots: `screenshots/title4.png`, `screenshots/game7.png`.
2. Re-test start position and initial survivor visibility after recent world-camera/ring changes.
3. Force-simulate 60–130 seconds via `window.__HORDE__` to verify level-up cards, boss spawn, boss bar, victory, and defeat UI.
4. Test mobile viewport (e.g. 390×844) and touch controls.
5. Fix any remaining visual/balance issues and re-check browser console.
6. Consider slightly reducing CSS grain/fog cost if performance matters.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: game shell and all overlays/HUD markup; loads scripts in order.
- `styles.css`: full visual design, responsive/mobile styling, title/HUD/overlay CSS.
- `js/core.js`: utilities, DOM refs, audio engine, procedural background builder, resizing, ambient motes.
- `js/world.js`: game state initialization, combat, AI, spawning, camera-independent world logic, upgrades application, HUD updates.
- `js/render.js`: camera rendering, all sprites/effects/title diorama, boss bar, frame rendering.
- `js/main.js`: upgrade card definitions, UI wiring, input, camera follow, game loop, debug export.
- `screenshots/title4.png`: latest title screenshot.
- `screenshots/game7.png`: latest gameplay screenshot.
- `start.sh`: serves the static site through the runtime.
- `/tmp/horde-server.log`: tmux-hosted server log, currently on `http://localhost:3002`.

## Important Context
- Server is running in tmux session `horde` via `PORT=3002 ./start.sh`; URL `http://localhost:3002`.
- `window.__HORDE__ = { H, state }` is exposed for debugging/capture automation.
- Current run constants: `H.RUN_TIME = 180`, `H.START_HORDE = 30`, boss at elapsed 120s.
- Camera: `H.camera = { x, y, zoom, initialized }`; desktop 1440px zoom is `1.42`, mobile narrower zoom `1.03`.
- World size: `H.WW = max(W*1.65, 1200)`, `H.WH = max(H*1.55, 900)`.
- Main loop `dt` cap is now `0.12`; at 8 FPS gameplay time approximates real time.
- Recent initial spawn ring radius is `Math.min(H.WW, H.WH) * 0.085`; player starts at `H.WW*0.51, H.WH*0.56`; Dawnfire at `H.WW*0.53, H.WH*0.515`.
- `titleBackgroundCanvas` is screen-sized; `backgroundCanvas` is world-sized; game background is drawn via camera crop for performance.
- No commits made; working tree has untracked `index.html`, `styles.css`, `js/`, `screenshots/`, plus pre-existing untracked scripts/README changes.

- After spawn: `state.spawnTimer = Math.max(1.3, 4.0 - elapsed / 65) + rand(0, 1.1);` At 0:4-5.1; at 30:3.5-4.6; at 60:3.1-4.2; at 120:2.2-3.3.
- base count = `1 + Math.floor(elapsed / 30)` at 30=2, 60=3, 90=4, 120=5; clamp max 5. So at 30s groups of 2-3; at 120 5-6. That's more. Combined shorter interval, active survivors 8-15. Good.
- alive threshold <24.
This may make the game harder but more fun, and XP/levels rise faster. It also makes boss encounter at 120 with higher level/more bats. Good. Need rebalance after simulation.

Actually `spawnCount` also counts survivors over the run, maybe 100+. Fine.

Let's implement and simulate with the optimal bot and random bot. Need be careful not to overdo difficulty. The horde can kill weak survivors quickly, and each kill heals. More enemies = more food, so it may be easier and more engaging.

Game10 shows player far from campfire at bottom; fire at bottom edge, empty right side. It's not terrible; dark game with trees. But maybe too empty. Also there is a weird large gray "DEVOURED" text at z? Actually text at x615,y229 "THE HUNT BEGINS" banner faded plus "DEVOURED" at y297. Fine. The campfire is partly offscreen, and no enemies. The player likely is moving top-right because bot. A human might be near campfire.

The key issue is spawn distribution: we spawn around player at screen edge, but if player moves, they may not see them until they catch up. The horde moves 252 vs squires 88, so catching up takes seconds. The game wants the player to hunt defenders; speed advantage lets you choose engagements. Empty moments are okay. But a horde game should feel livelier.

We can spawn groups "ahead" of the player's movement, not random 360. Current spawnGroup random angle around the current player. If the player is moving toward top-right at 252, a group spawned behind will never be seen. If spawn ahead, they intercept. Change spawn direction to biased toward current movement:
```
const mv = Math.hypot(h.vx,h.vy);
const a = mv > 40 ? Math.atan2(h.vy,h.vx) + rand(-1.2,1.2) : rand(0,TAU);
```
This ensures spawns in front. Combined with camera semi-lead (camera looks 0.13*vx ~33px), the new enemies appear ahead. Good. It also means if idle, spawn around. This improves encounter rate without increasing spawn count.

Also could spawn at slightly closer reach (reachX + 40) so they appear sooner. But offscreen edge is fine.
